put.description: M1.3 only. Resolve the stable identity first: identical purchaseId/sku/quantity returns the existing reservation, including terminal state and original price/deadline, without reallocation or renewed TTL. Conflicting payload or another reservation ID for that purchase returns a distinct 409 code. For a new reservation, obtain authoritative catalog price, perform checked positive int64 multiplication, then atomically allocate stock and persist the result. Overflow returns 400 MONETARY_OVERFLOW with no stock/reservation side effect. Unknown SKU is 404. No caller amount, expiry, or remote database access. Valid requests rejected with ITEM_NOT_FOUND, MONETARY_OVERFLOW or INSUFFICIENT_STOCK durably retain original identity, purchase binding, canonical payload, status and code before acknowledgement. Identical rejected replays preserve that error despite catalog/stock changes. No stock/reservation side effect permits rejection metadata only. GET may remain 404 if no Reservation exists. Retain identity protection without automatic deletion.

put.description: M1.3 only. COMMITTED replay is 200 even after expiresAt and never moves stock again. RELEASED returns 409 RESERVATION_RELEASED. EXPIRED or ACTIVE at/after authoritative expiresAt returns 409 RESERVATION_EXPIRED and cannot commit. ACTIVE can transition only at a serialized decision point with fresh database time strictly before expiresAt, after any contention wait. At exact equality expiry wins; terminal states never change. Detailed locking/expiry materialization is deferred. Any materialized EXPIRED stock cleanup commits before the 409 acknowledgement; exception handling must not roll it back.

put.description: M1.3 only. Release ACTIVE before expiry to RELEASED once; at/after expiry return EXPIRED after establishing cleanup. Existing RELEASED or EXPIRED replays return 200 unchanged; COMMITTED returns 409 RESERVATION_COMMITTED. Never move stock twice or change terminal state. Detailed atomic transition algorithm is M1.3. Stock cleanup commits before acknowledgement.

Problem.description: RFC 9457-style response. HTTP status and status member must agree. code and violations are Aegis extensions. Never expose SQL, credentials, or stack traces. Consumers must tolerate unknown extension fields.

unitPriceMinor.description: Positive signed 64-bit integer minor units when present; range 1..9223372036854775807. No float, wraparound, saturation, rounding, or negative/zero amount. Nullable fields allow null only as explicitly constrained by the containing schema.

observedAt.description: Finite UTC RFC 3339 instant, supported years 0001..9999. No infinity; cross-field ordering is a persistence/runtime invariant.

CatalogItem.description: Inventory is catalog and price authority. Availability is a snapshot, never a stock allocation guarantee.

ReservationRequest.description: positive quantity within int32. Inventory computes total using checked int64 multiplication of authoritative unitPriceMinor and quantity, before allocation. Nonpositive/out-of-range input is 400 INVALID_REQUEST; product overflow is 400 MONETARY_OVERFLOW with no mutation. Existing identical reservation replays return original snapshot instead of recomputing using catalog changes.

unitPriceMinor.description: Positive signed 64-bit integer minor units when present; range 1..9223372036854775807. No float, wraparound, saturation, rounding, or negative/zero amount. Nullable fields allow null only as explicitly constrained by the containing schema.

totalAmountMinor.description: Positive signed 64-bit integer minor units when present; range 1..9223372036854775807. No float, wraparound, saturation, rounding, or negative/zero amount. Nullable fields allow null only as explicitly constrained by the containing schema.

expiresAt.description: UTC database-authoritative deadline, immutable for the reservation; no renewal endpoint. expiresAt > createdAt. New commit at or after this instant is forbidden. Finite UTC RFC 3339 instant, supported years 0001..9999. No infinity; cross-field ordering is a persistence/runtime invariant.

createdAt.description: Finite UTC RFC 3339 instant, supported years 0001..9999. No infinity; cross-field ordering is a persistence/runtime invariant.

Reservation.description: M1.3 only. Exactly one terminal state: COMMITTED, RELEASED, EXPIRED; terminal states never change. totalAmountMinor equals the checked positive int64 product of quantity and unitPriceMinor. Inventory chooses and persists expiresAt from database time. ACTIVE is a persisted nonterminal state, not a guarantee of current eligibility: if expiry processing lags, GET may return ACTIVE with a past deadline. New commit must evaluate fresh authoritative database time at its serialized decision point after any contention wait: eligible iff state is ACTIVE and decisionTime < expiresAt. Equality is expired. Never use a stale transaction-start timestamp for this decision. A committed transition before the deadline remains valid even if acknowledgement arrives afterward. Algorithms/SQL and deadline duration remain M1.3 design.
x-aegis-semantic-invariants: COMMITTED replay remains 200 after the deadline; no second stock movement.
GET does not itself promise expiry cleanup has run. Expiry/release reclaim stock exactly once under concurrency.
An uncommitted expired reservation cannot later commit even if an expiry worker has not persisted EXPIRED.
